title: Context Watermark + Async Snapshotter for Stable Request Identity Across Forks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As we instrument more async-first SDKs and server frameworks, we see fractured sampling decisions, duplicated spans, and lost provenance when requests fork (background jobs, streaming fibers, websockets). Existing hooks propagate headers and basic IDs but lack a compact, monotonic marker and a lightweight snapshot mechanism to rehydrate minimal context in detached execution paths.

Goal: Implement a compact request "watermark" that travels with the carrier and an async snapshotter API in SDKs that can capture a small deterministic context blob (stable request id, watermark, parent sampling decision, minimal metadata) and reinstate it in forked or delayed workers. This should reduce duplicated traces, align sampling across forks, and enable accurate cost/trace attribution for long-lived or multi-path requests.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change sampling algorithms themselves, nor does it introduce heavyweight provenance signatures (those are a follow-up). We also won't modify server ingress authentication for this work.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs expose a cross-language AsyncSnapshot API that returns a compact base64 blob <= 128 bytes
A deterministic 64-bit Context Watermark is generated for every new top-level request and included in all outgoing carriers
When an AsyncSnapshot is applied in a detached worker, traces produced show a single coherent request id and causal linkage in Jaeger/Zipkin UI
End-to-end test that simulates request forking (HTTP handler -> background job + websocket) shows single trace with no duplicated root spans and sampling decision preserved
Latency dashboards show no >1% increase in p95 for instrumented endpoints after rollout
Backwards compatibility: legacy clients without snapshot support degrade to existing header-only propagation (no errors)
Documentation and SDK migration guide published in dev portal
technical_notes: Watermark format: 8-byte monotonic uint64 (timestamp ms high bits + 16-bit entropy low bits), encoded as hex string for carrier friendliness

AsyncSnapshot: JSON-lite with keys {rid, wm, sd, meta} where rid=stable request uuid v4, wm=hex watermark, sd=sampling decision enum, meta=minimal routing tags; compressed and base64-encoded to stay <128 bytes

SDK surface: snapshot() -> string, applySnapshot(string) -> ContextHandle; language bindings: node/python/go/java; implement fiber/async-safe storage (async_hooks/contextvars/goroutine local) depending on runtime

Middleware changes: HTTP/gRPC middleware attaches X-RD-Watermark and X-RD-Snapshot when snapshot size <= 128 bytes. For larger carriers, fallback to X-RD-Watermark only and log sample for investigation
Sampling: preserve existing sampling decision flag in snapshot (keep 'keep', 'drop', 'unsampled') but do not alter algorithm in this ticket
KV cache affinity: runtime can use watermark to prefer warm KV-cache shards for forked work in subsequent tickets (design note only)
Security: snapshot blob contains no secrets or user PII; still needs review for enterprise deployments (KMS/HSM considered in follow-up)
rollout_plan: Feature flag: rollout.rq_context_watermark; default off for all customers
Canary: enable for internal staging and 5% of requests from non-sensitive tenants for two days
Telemetry: add metric rd.sdk.snapshot_applied{ok|error}, rd.watermark_generated_count; add tracing tag rd.watermark.present
Full rollout if canary success and <0.5% increase in error/latency and no trace duplication alerts
SDK GA: release minor SDK versions with migration guide; mark legacy header-only code deprecated after 8 weeks
testing_plan: Unit tests for watermark generation edge cases (clock skew, concurrent requests)
Integration test harness that spawns N concurrent requests that fork into M background tasks and validates single-trace assembly
Load test at production QPS with and without snapshot to measure p95/p99 impact
Compatibility tests: legacy agent + new server and new agent + legacy server matrix
End-to-end visual verification in staging Jaeger trace UI and console dashboards

2025-02-12 Liam O'Connor: Spike completed for Node + Python SDKs. Prototype watermark generator implemented. Observed 0.6% p95 increase under synthetic load; needs optimization.
